newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB denies it more restrictive on Swiss money mkt.
newsitem.headline: SNB denies it more restrictive on Swiss money mkt.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank said a rise in short-term Swiss franc deposit rates on Wednesday was not a result of any shift at the central bank to a more restrictive monetary policy.
"We have not become more restrictive," a SNB spokesman told Reuters when asked if the bank had any influence on the money market rate increase.
"This is a result of technical market factors," he added.
Tommorow/next money was up to 2.00/2.50 in afternoon trade after starting around 1.75-1.88. Overnight was also up strongly to 2.00-3.00.
The SNB spokesman noted that the year-end, which is also a quarter-end, was nearing and that the end of the reporting period could play a role in tighter supply.
Money market dealers also downplayed any idea the SNB could be tightening money supply, arguing this would make no sense as the slumping Swiss economy still showed no signs of recovery.
One dealer said the hike was a technical distortion resulting from big U.S. hedge funds buying Swiss franks.
"The funds are buying francs through tomorrow/next and local banks are replenishing their supply from overnight money," the Zurich-based dealer said.
"There is enough liquidity in the market, it is just a problem of distribution," he added.
The SNB spokesman declined to comment when asked by Reuters whether the central bank saw any need to supply additional liquidity to the money market.
Another dealer said he saw no reason on the central bank's part for rates to rise.
He played down talk that the SNB could be nearing the end of its generous monetary policy and nudging rates higher to head off inflationary pressure.
"The economy is in such bad shape that they would not do this, and certainly not in December," he said.
